Series::LinearAlgAccessor::mv¶

Back to Series::LinearAlgAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series Series::LinearAlgAccessor::mv(const Series& vector) const
Series SeriesLinearAlgProxy::mv() const
Series Series::mv(const Series& vector) const

What It Does¶

mv() multiplies one rank-2 matrix by one rank-1 vector. For a matrix with shape [m, k] and vector with shape [k], the result has shape [m]:

out[i] = sum(matrix[i, t] * vector[t], over t)

Each matrix row contributes one scalar, so the number of rows becomes the output length. The column dimension is paired with the vector and contracted.

Rows As Dot Products¶

The vector supplies weights for the matrix’s columns. Multiplying by [1, 0, 0] selects the first column; multiplying by [0, 0, 1] selects the third. General vectors form weighted combinations of all columns.

This column-combination view and the equivalent row-dot-product view describe the same computation. Use whichever makes the surrounding algorithm easier to reason about.

Parameter¶

vector (const Series&) The rank-1 right operand. Its length must equal the matrix’s column count, and its dtype and platform must match the matrix.

Returns¶

Series A new rank-1 Series with shape [matrix.size(0)]. The matrix and vector are unchanged.

Gradient¶

For y = A x and incoming vector sensitivity g = dL/dy:

dL/dA = outer(g, x)
dL/dx = A^T g

Every output sensitivity scales one copy of x into the corresponding matrix row. The vector sensitivity gathers contributions from every matrix row.

Examples¶

Example 1. Compute one row-vector inner product per matrix row.

auto matrix = pluss::make_series({
    {2.0, 0.0, -1.0},
    {1.0, 3.0, 2.0},
});
auto vector = pluss::make_series({4.0, 5.0, 6.0});

std::cout << matrix.linearalg.mv(vector) << "\n";

The rows produce 2*4 + 0*5 - 1*6 = 2 and 1*4 + 3*5 + 2*6 = 31.

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[2, 31]

Example 2. Basis vectors expose the column-combination interpretation.

auto matrix = pluss::make_series({
    {2.0, -1.0, 4.0},
    {0.0, 3.0, 5.0},
});

std::cout << "first_column="
          << matrix.linearalg.mv(pluss::make_series({1.0, 0.0, 0.0}))
          << "\n";
std::cout << "third_column="
          << matrix.linearalg.mv(pluss::make_series({0.0, 0.0, 1.0}))
          << "\n";

Output¶

first_column=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[2, 0]
third_column=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[4, 5]

Example 3. Reverse a summed matrix-vector product through both operands.

auto matrix = pluss::make_series({{1.0, 2.0}, {3.0, 4.0}});
auto vector = pluss::make_series({5.0, 6.0});
matrix.tracks_slope_(true);
vector.tracks_slope_(true);

matrix.linearalg.mv(vector).sum().reverse();

std::cout << "dL_dmatrix=" << matrix.sensitivity() << "\n";
std::cout << "dL_dvector=" << vector.sensitivity() << "\n";

The incoming sensitivity is [1, 1]. Its outer product with the vector copies [5, 6] into each matrix row. A^T [1, 1] sums the matrix columns to [4, 6].

Output¶

dL_dmatrix=pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[5, 6],
  [5, 6]]
dL_dvector=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[4, 6]

Example 4 (contract check). Two vectors are a dot() case, not an mv() case.

try {
  std::cout << pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0}).linearalg.mv(
      pluss::make_series({3.0, 4.0})) << "\n";
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::cout << e.what() << "\n";
}

Output¶

mv: expected a 2D matrix and a 1D vector

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The left operand must have rank 2 and the right operand rank 1.

  • The matrix column count must equal the vector length.

  • mv() does not broadcast a vector across matrix batches; use matmul() when batching is intentional.

  • Dtypes and platforms must match.

  • Operand order is fixed: vector-by-matrix multiplication is a different matmul() rank pattern.

Summary¶

mv() is a strict matrix-by-vector operation. It contracts columns against vector positions and returns one value per matrix row.
